questions.q: What HTTP status code does a successful record creation through the REST API return?
questions.explain: A successful POST to /sobjects/{Type} returns 201 Created along with the new record's id in the response body.

questions.q: What does a successful PATCH update to an existing record return?
options: 204 No Content, with an empty body
200 OK, with the full updated record in the body
questions.explain: Updates and deletes both return 204 No Content on success — an empty body, following Salesforce's REST API convention.

questions.q: What happens if you send a PATCH update with only one field in the body, e.g. just { "Phone": "..." }?
options: Only that field is changed; every other field on the record is left untouched
Every other field on the record is reset to blank
The request fails because all fields must be included
questions.explain: PATCH updates are partial — only the fields you include in the body are changed, and everything else on the record stays as it was.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an upsert operation using an external ID field?
options: It inserts a new record if no match on that field exists (201 Created), or updates the existing one if a match is found (204 No Content) — in a single operation
It permanently deletes any record matching that field value
It only works for custom objects, never standard objects
It requires you to already know the Salesforce record ID
questions.explain: Upsert matches on a designated external ID field rather than the Salesforce record ID, letting an integration avoid separate insert-or-update logic.

questions.q: Which URL pattern correctly performs an upsert by an external ID field named Legacy_System_Id__c with value LS-00482?
questions.explain: Upsert by external ID uses PATCH against /sobjects/{Type}/{externalIdFieldName}/{value} — the same verb as a regular update, but addressed by the external ID field and value instead of the record ID.
